newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices rise on lower arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices rise on lower arrivals.

text.p: Indian cotton prices gained on Monday on lower arrivals despite low mill demand, dealers said.
"Old crop inflows were low due to the tail end of the season and new crop arrivals are yet to pick up," one trader said.
In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan (medium staple) rose by 300 rupees to 13,500/13,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).

Bengal-deshi ready delivery moved up by 25/30 rupees to 845/870 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while forward delivery climbed up 40/50 rupees to 900/925 rupees. "Sentiment was encouraging at the close but looking at the sluggish physical enquiries, the market may come down again," he said.
